approved: Therapeutic Goods Amendment (Medicines Shortages and Other Measures) Bill 2026
Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
This bill would change the law to better manage medicine shortages and discontinuations in Australia.

It would require drug companies to notify the government at least 12 months before stopping supply of certain medicines, and give officials new powers to demand information about stock levels and shortages.
The bill would also let the regulator group similar biological medicines under a single registration entry, and move powers to inspect clinical trial sites from regulations into the main Act.
Requires sponsors to notify the Secretary at least 12 months before permanently discontinuing a reportable medicine.
Allows the Secretary to demand information from all sponsors about availability, shortages or discontinuations of their products.
Lets the Secretary define common biologicals groups so similar biologicals share a single Register entry.
Moves legal powers to enter and inspect clinical trial sites from delegated legislation to the primary Act.
Allows the Medicines Watch List to incorporate other documents as they change over time.
Sponsors of approved medicines, biological medicine manufacturers, and clinical trial operators.

Moved the Therapeutic Goods Amendment (Medicines Shortages and Other Measures) Bill 2026 for second reading, proposing stronger reporting of medicine discontinuations and availability, broader information-gathering powers, grouped entries for similar biologicals, clinical trial inspection powers, and updates to the Medicines Watch List.

Moved the Therapeutic Goods (Charges) Amendment Bill 2026 for second reading, proposing annual charges for grouped biologicals included in the Australian Register of Therapeutic Goods and stating that the measure would support related reforms while reducing industry costs and regulatory burden.

Declared that specified telecommunications, therapeutic goods, biosecurity, and wine legislation would stand referred to the Federation Chamber, either immediately or following adjournment of second-reading debates, unless otherwise ordered.

Moved a second reading amendment on two Therapeutic Goods bills, supporting earlier notification of medicine discontinuations and streamlined biologic registrations but arguing that more action is needed to address underlying shortages. The amendment called for a comprehensive policy to strengthen domestic manufacturing capacity and reduce shortages; the coalition would not oppose the bill and reserved its position on amendments.

Supported the Therapeutic Goods Amendment (Medicines Shortages and Other Measures) Bill 2026, which would require advance notice of permanent medicine discontinuations, expand information requests, streamline grouped biologicals and clarify clinical trial powers; amendments were negatived, the bill passed its second reading and was reported without amendment.
